- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or shows recent downward momentum, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to capture rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3%.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >2% for 3+ consecutive days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% smoothed) to dampen volatility.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model may misalign with trend; align forecast with sentiment direction but cap deviation at ±3% from recent 5-day average.
